slides.headline: A father. A knife. One second left.
slides.sub: Caravaggio, The Sacrifice of Isaac, about 1603

slides.headline: A test of faith
slides.text: In the Bible, God orders Abraham to sacrifice his only son, Isaac. Abraham obeys. Caravaggio paints the very last second.

slides.headline: The father
slides.text: Abraham pins the boy's head down on the stone with one hand. In the other, the knife is already at his throat.

slides.headline: The son
slides.text: Isaac's face is pressed against the rock, his mouth open in terror. He is a boy, and he knows what is coming.

slides.headline: The angel
slides.text: Then a young angel bursts in and grabs Abraham's wrist. Abraham turns, startled, the blade frozen in the air.

slides.headline: The ram
slides.text: Beside the boy, a ram waits. It will die instead. The angel's other hand points toward it: take the animal, not the child.

slides.headline: The same face?
slides.text: Now compare the angel and Isaac. X-rays suggest the same young model, Cecco, posed for both: the victim and the rescuer.

slides.headline: The old man
slides.text: Abraham shows no joy at being stopped, only shock. Caravaggio painted it for Cardinal Maffeo Barberini, the future Pope Urban VIII.

slides.headline: Faith or horror?
slides.text: Most painters showed calm obedience. Caravaggio shows a terrified child and a father ready to kill. Is this faith, or horror?
